statement.p: A car going at 20 \ \mathrm{ft/s} decelerates at a constant 4 \ \mathrm{ft/s^2} to come to a stop.
(a) Fill in the following table showing the velocity of the car every second. Fill in a zero velocity for any time after that at which the car comes to a rest.
(b) When does the car come to a stop?
Using your table, find left and right sums which estimate the total distance traveled before the car comes to rest. Which is an overestimate, and which is an underestimate?

(c) On a sheet of paper, sketch a graph of velocity against time. On the graph, show an area representing the distance traveled before the car comes to rest. Use the graph to calculate this distance.
(d) Now find a formula for the velocity of the car as a function of time:
and then find the total distance traveled by antidifferentiation.

static.solution:
(a) Since the velocity is constantly decreasing, every second its velocity decreases by 4 ft/s, so that the car stops after 5 seconds, and we have the time and speed values
t= 0 1 2 3 4 5 6
v= 20 16 12 8 4 0 0
(b) Over the interval a \leq t \leq a + 1, the left-hand velocity is v(a), and the right-hand velocity is v(a + 1). Since we are considering one-second intervals, \Delta t = 1, and n = 5. The left sum is then 60 ft, and the right sum is 40 ft. Thus the left sum is an overestimate and the right is an underestimate.
(c) Area A in the figure below represents distance traveled.
A = \frac12 (\mbox{base})(\mbox{height}) = \frac12 \cdot 20 \cdot 5 = 50 ft.
(d) The velocity is constantly decreasing at a rate of 4 ft/s, so after each second the velocity has dropped by 4 ft. Therefore v(t) = 20-4t.
An antiderivative for v(t) is s(t), where s(t) = 20 t - t^2. Thus by the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the distance traveled = s(5) - s(0) = 50 - 0 = 50 ft.
